problem: Navigation policies trained in simulators (e.g. Habitat) transfer poorly to the real world because of the appearance gap and missing sensor and actuator noise. Prior sim-to-real assessments need a real robot during training and test, or use only sparse grids of real images in simplified environments.
motivation: Collecting real-world RL experience is expensive and slow, so it is valuable to measure and reduce the sim-to-real gap entirely in simulation. The authors observe that a policy that navigates almost perfectly on virtual observations fails on real-world images of the same environment.
key_idea: Align a Matterport virtual mesh with a COLMAP SfM real-image model of the same office, so Habitat can replace virtual frames with the nearest real image at each step (plus Gaussian sensor and actuator noise), enabling training and evaluation on real observations without running real-world episodes.
insight: Table 1: a policy trained only on virtual data reaches 2.2% SR on real observations, versus 85.9% when trained on real observations. Virtual pre-training followed by real fine-tuning gives the best result (97.0% SR), so simulation knowledge does transfer. Unsupervised CycleGAN adaptation helps (33.1% SR) but leaves a large gap, and combining it with real data adds nothing. Noise-aware training recovers much of the loss on virtual observations (large sensor and actuator noise: SR 16.2 to 27.9) but hurts on real observations, so simple noise training is not enough.
method: Two 3D models: a Matterport virtual mesh (accurate geometry, limited photo-realism) and a COLMAP SfM real model built from 24,896 robot-collected RGB images with camera poses.
Alignment: COLMAP model_aligner registers the real model to the virtual coordinate frame, using 6K Habitat-rendered virtual images with known poses as the reference set.

Real-observation episode generation: Habitat runs on the virtual mesh, and at each step the 6DoF pose is reduced to 3DoF (X, Z, yaw). FAISS retrieval first filters by yaw cosine similarity (threshold 0.96), then picks the nearest X-Z image, which is fed to the policy.
Noise models: Gaussian localization-sensor noise (0.2m/7° to 0.8m/30°) and actuation noise (0.05m/5° to 0.2m/20°). Medium actuation noise was measured on the Sanbot Elf robot.

Policy and adaptation: RGB DD-PPO PointGoal agent pre-trained on Gibson and MP3D. It is fine-tuned on virtual data, real data, CycleGAN-translated virtual images (50 epochs, 5k images per domain), or combinations. Noise fine-tuning freezes the visual encoder.

setting.backbone: RGB DD-PPO (visual encoder + 2 recurrent layers), pre-trained on Gibson+MP3D, then fine-tuned with RL
setting.training_data: Virtual Habitat frames (1.2M-2.4M) from a Matterport scan of a 150 m² office; real-image frames (train half of 24,896 images) for fine-tuning; CycleGAN on 5k virtual + 5k real images
setting.observation: monocular RGB 256x256 + relative goal coordinates + previous action
setting.action_space: discrete: forward 0.25 m, turn left 10°, turn right 10°, STOP
setting.simulator: Habitat (custom office scene with real-image retrieval)
setting.privileged: none at test time (perfect or noisy localization/GPS provides the goal coordinates)

numbers.eval_set_note: 1000 sampled episodes in the 150 m² office; real-image test half
numbers.extra: 200 step limit; 0.20 m success radius; no noise; 1.2M virtual + 1.2M real frames
numbers.evidence: Table 1 Virtual to Real Policy Transfer, row Virtual+real

numbers.extra: 2.4M virtual frames; tested on real observations
1.2M virtual + 1.2M CycleGAN-translated frames; no real labels

numbers_note: The paper's benchmark is its own single-office environment, not a standard benchmark. The noise-table results (virtual and real observations) are not listed as separate entries; they include e.g. real, large noise trained with noise SPL 0.0827 / SR 0.1180.
results: On real observations, a virtual-only policy gets 2.2% SR and 0.0160 SPL. CycleGAN adaptation raises it to about 33-34% SR, and virtual pre-training plus real fine-tuning reaches 97.0% SR and 0.8001 SPL (better than real-only at 85.9% SR). Sensor and actuator noise sharply reduce performance (real SPL 0.8001 to 0.1467 at large noise). Training with noise helps on virtual observations but degrades results on real ones.
limitations: Only a single 150 m² office with one robot and a single retrieval-based real-image simulation, which limits view coverage; images are the nearest ones (yaw filtered at cosine 0.96) rather than novel views.
Noise models are simple Gaussian localization/actuation noise; the tool was not validated by real-robot deployment, and noise-aware training hurt on real observations.
Only RGB PointGoal DD-PPO with basic adaptation (CycleGAN, fine-tuning) was tested; real train/test images come from the same trajectories of the same environment.
